title: Yosef ben Simai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Shabbat 121a relates that he was the king’s steward. When a fire broke out in his courtyard on Shabbat, the soldiers of Tzippori’s garrison came to extinguish it. He did not let them, and a miracle occurred: rain fell and put out the fire. Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat there, Yoma 8:5 and Nedarim 4:9 call him Yose ben Simai. Yevamot 115a relates that two scholars were traveling by ship with Abba Yose ben Simai; the ship sank, and Rabbi permitted their wives to remarry. Possibly he is Yosef ben Simai. Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 15:5 has Abba (bar) Simi.

notes.text: Gistra is rendered as the garrison. Yosef, Yose, Abba Yose and Abba (bar) Simi remain separate reported forms; their identification is Hyman’s possibility.

The consulted Shabbat 121a directly names Yosef ben Simai and the Tzippori garrison. Its closing discussion says he need not have prevented their extinguishing the fire. The supplied account is retained; it does not establish the identity of Yosef, Yose, Abba Yose or Abba (bar) Simi in the other cited episodes.
